newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia caiman declared in danger of extinction.
newsitem.headline: Colombia caiman declared in danger of extinction.

text.p: Colombia has declared a species of crocodile "in danger of extinction" because it has been decimated by hunting and shrinking natural habitat, government officials said on Wednesday.

The so-called plains caiman, Crocodylus Intermedius, lives in the Orinoco Basin region which stretches from eastern Colombia into Venezuela. Of 28 different subspecies recorded in 1995, only two now survive, an Environment Ministry spokesman said.
The ministry called on Bogota's National University and experts at a research institute to draw up a conservation plan for the caiman.
The reptile can grow to 22 feet (seven metres) long and has been traditionally hunted -- legally or illegally -- for its skin. Farmers have encroached on the wetlands where it lives.
This week's official designation of the crocodile as in danger was the first of its kind by Colombia for any of its native fauna, the ministry spokesman said.
